---

1. Problem

👉 Hindi + English mix (local audience ke liye)

* Kya-kya missing hai jo Google rank ke liye zaroori hai
* Kya-kya add karna compulsory hai
* Kya-kya ignore kar rahe ho jo competitors nahi kar rahe

1. Website Overview (simple words)
2. Extracted Content (tables)
3. SEO Audit Report

5. Content Suggestions (copy-paste ready)

When your doctor prescribes a blood test, they often mention the word "fasting". But have you ever wondered why? Is skipping your morning tea really that important?

At National Diagnostic Center, we believe informed patients make better health decisions. Here is everything you need to know about fasting before a blood test.

What does fasting really mean?

Fasting for a blood test means you should not eat or drink anything except water for a specific period, usually 8-12 hours. This ensures that your blood creates a "baseline" reading, unaffected by the nutrients and sugars from your last meal.

Which tests require fasting?

  • Fasting Blood Glucose: Used to diagnose diabetes. Food intake directly spikes sugar levels.
  • Lipid Profile: Measures cholesterol and triglycerides. Fats from food can stay in your blood for hours, giving falsely high triglyceride readings.
  • Vitamin B12 & Iron Studies: Some doctors recommend fasting for these to get accurate absorption levels.
  • Thyroid Function Tests: While not strictly always fasting, taking the sample in the morning on an empty stomach is often recommended for consistency, especially for TSH levels.

What happens if I eat?

If you eat before a fasting test, your results might show higher than normal glucose or fat levels. This could lead to:

  • A false diagnosis of Diabetes or High Cholesterol.
  • Unnecessary medication prescriptions.
  • The need to repeat the test (wasting your time and money).

Tips for a smooth fasting experience

1. Drink Water: Staying hydrated makes it easier for the phlebotomist to find your veins.
2. Time it right: Sleep through most of your fasting window. If you sleep at 11 PM and wake up at 7 AM, you are already 8 hours into your fast!
3. Avoid Alcohol & Smoking: These can drastically alter liver enzymes and glucose levels.
